gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-carian: Graceful and stencil-flat, Bevellier hugs its letters close together. Noto Sans Carian keeps its terminals apart like open scissor blades, so paragraphs of text keep breathing easily down the column.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Stencil-flat and tightly spaced: Bevellier has no thick-thin shifts at all. Noto Sans Chakma stays approachable, its s and c open and uncrowded, so a full page of reading goes down easily.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-cham: Bevellier's round bowls keep walls of unvarying thickness all the way round. Noto Sans Cham, a modern sans below, offers open c shapes and tall rounded lowercase forms for the text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Bevellier looks drawn with a single pen tip, flat and stencil-cut. Noto Sans Cherokee sets a tall band of letters beneath short stalks, with an e whose terminal gapes, so text runs smoothly.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Bevellier never shifts from heavy to light within a stroke, stencil-flat throughout. Noto Sans Chorasmian has a large x-height, short ascenders and curves that stop short of closing, so lines move along comfortably.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Bevellier's strokes look like bent paperclips, flat and tightly spaced. That wiry display character is made for big, brief moments, while Noto Sans Coptic lets a middle-heavy texture carry the longer reading.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-cuneiform: Sophisticated in a flat, stencil-cut way, Bevellier hums along at one constant line weight. And it earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Cuneiform opens its e and puffs out its lowercase like glass beads.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Flat, stencil-cut and snug: Bevellier has no thick-thin swing. Noto Sans Deseret echoes Bevellier's high, wide-looking lowercase and squat ascenders, and that shared stance is what holds the two together.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Bevellier is stencil-flat, with crossbars as fat as the stems they join. Noto Sans Duployan is the one for text, with a wide mouth on its a and oversized counters, where Bevellier is for display.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Noto Sans Elbasan reads big-bodied and contemporary, its terminals never pinching. Above it, Bevellier's glyphs look cut from strips of equal width, and the text below runs on with little friction.
